newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SAirGroup seen with 1st H1 profit in 1990s.
newsitem.headline: SAirGroup seen with 1st H1 profit in 1990s.

text.p: SAirGroup is expected to report half-year profits on Thursday for the first time this decade, confirming that the Swiss airline services group has finally taken off.

Investors have already enjoyed a sky-high ride this year and analysts are confident SAirGroup's shares can soar even higher as the benefits of recent cost-cutting and restructuring continue to improve the group's profitability.
"For the first time the SAirGroup will confirm that it is on the right track," said Beat Kunz of Bank Julius Baer.
On average analysts expect SAirGroup, which includes the Swissair airline, to report a first-half operating profit of 168 million Swiss francs ($110.8 million) and a net profit of 65 million.
The forecasts for net profit range from a low of 10 million francs to a high of 100 million, reflecting the fundamental volatility and difficulty in forecasting airlines' earnings.

In the first half of 1996 SAirGroup reported a net loss of 51 million, continuing its tradition of first-half losses since 1990 as Swissair normally earns the bulk of its money during the heavy business travel months of September and October.
But in contrast to recent years, analysts are confident and more relaxed about SAirGroup this year, reflecting improved transparency and confidence in the group's management.
"It will be a strong set of numbers," said Andrew Barker of SBC Warburg, noting there should be very little scope for disappoinment at the operating level given cost-cutting.

SAirGroup executives have recently commented on the group being ahead of budget in the first four months of the year and outlined management's target of a 600 million Swiss franc operating profit for 1997 after reaching 155 million in the first four months.

"The company officials would not have made these statements if it were not the case, but the market still wants to see if they are achieving it," said Charles Donald of Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS).
In addition to the benefits from cost-cutting, SAirGroup has also benefitted from good traffic and improving economies, trends that were confirmed by recent strong results from KLM and SAS.
In June, for example, Swissair's seat load factor rose to 74.3 percent from 67.7 percent last year.
In May SAirGroup confirmed business was on the upswing and forecast a "marked" improvement in operating profit.

The turnaround in SAirGroup's profitability has come from chief executive Philippe Bruggisser's two-pronged strategy of cutting costs at the core Swissair airline -- the achilles' heel of the group -- and raising revenue.
The aim is to improve the group's bottom line by 500 million francs by 1998, including 100 million francs in personnel costs that is being achieved by cutting jobs and reducing salaries.
Most of the cost-cutting measures were initiated last year, but are first really starting to bite this year.
While analysts have few doubts that cost-cutting is helping improve results, the questions are on the revenue side and the effects of focusing and expanding the Zurich hub.

Good first-half figures have been discounted by the stock market, where SAirGroup's shares have soared 74 percent this year to close at 1,880 francs on Monday, the strongest performer among Europe's airlines.
"The result can only be positive, but the share has already discounted that," said Dieter Winet of Societe Generale.
However, analysts remain bullish in the long term. "Even at this level,
the share is extremely cheap," said Barker of SBC Warburg.
-- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340 ($ = 1.516 Swiss Francs)
